Use Tier 2: replace the current uniformly sampled negative objective with mixed hard-negative ranking, keeping the architecture and data pipeline fixed. The latest trial reached macro validation HR@10 of 0.5025 versus the best 0.5375, with Electronics at 0.395, so the recent representation and weighting changes have not resolved the plateau. A plausible limitation is that uniform negatives provide too little supervision for distinguishing relevant items from plausible competing recommendations.

Modify model_design by scoring 128 uniformly sampled, training-unseen candidate negatives per sequence and selecting the 16 highest-scoring negatives separately at each valid position. Combine these with 16 independently sampled uniform negatives in the existing cross-entropy objective, retaining its positive target and temporal aggregation weights. Select hard-negative indices using detached scores, then compute the selected logits through learned embeddings so gradients update both the sequence representation and competing items. Exclude the user's complete training history from both negative pools; validation interactions must never influence training sampling.

Modify training_evaluation only to integrate this objective, preserving the current backbone, preference branch, optimizer, seeds, splits, and four-category routing for a controlled experiment. Select checkpoints using fixed validation HR@10 with 200 users and 99 unique negatives per category, and compare the independently evaluated macro score against 0.5375. Keep inference and the predictor writer aligned with the unchanged trained architecture, and let the host perform held-out inference without reading test files. This experiment tests whether stronger discrimination among confusing candidates improves top-10 retrieval while retaining uniform negatives to limit concentration on potentially ambiguous hard examples.
